AI agents just ran a nation-state intrusion. 🤖

Microsoft says China-aligned Storm-0940 used ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent AI pentest framework, after compromising ConnectWise's Cloud Backup app.

→ Stolen app identities gave trusted access to customer tenants, with no user sign-in
→ The agents attempted sign-ins at 2,250+ Microsoft 365 tenants

What to check today:
✅ Find ConnectWise app IDs in Entra (search by app ID, not display name)
✅ Review service-principal sign-ins back to 1 Oct
✅ Alert on apps adding credentials or assigning themselves roles

Is your SOC watching app identities as closely as user identities? 👇

cover.sub: A test account nobody had touched in 12 years. 3,300 people's data, mostly children's.

slides.title: The door nobody remembered
slides.body: Attackers used “Test 2”, a test account that had existed for more than 12 years. Its only protection was the password Password1.

slides.label: stolen before the ransomware ran
slides.note: Then 182.7 GB encrypted across file and SQL servers

slides.title: Who got hurt
slides.body: Data Cymru, a Welsh government-funded data unit, and its IT provider. 3,300 people affected, mostly children in family-support projects. The attack hit in November 2024.

slides.title: The ICO's verdict
slides.body: Both reprimanded under UK GDPR, no fine. Failures: weak password rules, no audits of accounts, no review of local admin accounts, and a missing data-processing contract.

slides.title: Do this Monday
items: Hunt stale and test accounts in AD; disable what nobody owns
Require MFA on every remote access path
Write security duties into every outsourcing contract

items.ig_caption:
Third time since July. 🚨

Arista disclosed CVE-2026-114625 (CVSS 9.9), a SQL injection zero-day in VeloCloud Orchestrator, the SD-WAN management plane. Attackers exploited it before a patch existed.

→ A low-privilege (Enterprise Read Only) account can escalate to operator control
→ That reaches managed data, the VCO host and downstream Edge devices
→ Fixed in 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10 and 6.4.2.12 (Arista patched cloud-hosted VCOs itself)

Patch, then restrict the VCO web UI to trusted admin networks and review admin activity.

Three zero-days in one management plane in four months. Would you still expose it to the internet? 👇

Source: Arista Security Advisory 0199, via Aviatrix Threat Research (22 Oct 2026)

cover.hook: The alerts fired. A tool closed them as false positives.
cover.sub: How a China-linked group sat inside BeyondTrust for a month before anyone looked.

slides.label: from first exploit (29 Aug) to discovery (28 Sep)

slides.title: The flaw
slides.body: CVE-2026-102764 (CVSS 9.3): an unauthenticated zero-day in self-hosted BeyondTrust Remote Support up to 26.2.3. Google and Mandiant tie it to ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage group.

slides.title: What they did inside
slides.body: A PHP web shell, root via a SUID shell copy, passwordless sudo for persistence, attempts to dump the credential vault, a dozen-plus logs deleted, and a custom SOCKS5 tunneler.

slides.title: The real lesson
slides.body: BeyondTrust's sensors did fire. A third-party detection platform's triage tool closed the alerts as false positives. Automated triage that nobody samples is a blind spot.

slides.title: If you run Remote Support
items: Treat exposed vulnerable appliances as compromised until reviewed
Snapshot before any reboot; rebuild from a clean image
Rotate credentials after patching, not before

items.question: Who reviews the alerts your automation closes?
